inspection_steps: Check if current is going into the batteries.
Make sure batteries are air-cooled.

maintenance_steps: Check the general condition of the cables at the bottom of the tower.
Replace worn cables when necessary.
Correct wrong cable connections when found.
Protect rusty cable clamps with grease.
inspection_steps: Check cable clamps.
Check cable connections.
Check the connections in the junction box.
safety_warnings: Live power cables can create a risk of electric shock.

maintenance_steps: Check the tower and related parts for wear and corrosion.
Check the cables at the bottom of the tower.
inspection_steps: Check the distance between blade tips and the tower.
Check flange tightness.
Check the connections in the junction box.
Check the tail pivot system.
safety_warnings: Do not stay below the tower during lowering or raising.

maintenance_steps: Repair holes and cracks when found.
Store removed blades safely.
inspection_steps: Inspect blades for cracks, holes, and other damage.
Inspect the leading edge.
Inspect blade roots.
Check the distance between blade tips and the tower.

maintenance_steps: Store the rotor in a clean, dry place away from metal components.
Replace corroded magnets when necessary.
inspection_steps: Check the rotor for cracks in the resin structure.
Check for friction between rotor and stator.
Check for wires with missing enamel.
safety_warnings: Never put fingers between rotor disks because they can be pinched.

inspection_steps: Check the stator for cracks in the resin structure.
Check for friction between the rotor and stator.
Check for wires with missing enamel.

maintenance_steps: Replace magnets if they are corroded.
Use epoxy resin when replacing magnets.
inspection_steps: Check if magnets are corroded.
safety_warnings: Permanent magnet generators have a powerful magnetic field.

inspection_steps: Check the daily, monthly, or annual yield on the inverter screen.
Check if the values are correct compared with average wind speed.
Check error messages on the inverter.

maintenance_steps: Protect rusty guy wires with car oil or plant oil.
Tighten guy wires when necessary.
inspection_steps: Check guy wires for wear and corrosion.
Check if shackles and turnbuckles are secure.

maintenance_steps: Replace both roller bearings at the same time when needed.
Tighten the nut, spin the hub, then slack it off slightly to reduce stress on the bearing.
inspection_steps: Check for play in the hub.
Check if the hub bearing is stuck.

maintenance_steps: Check that anchor points are secure.
Secure a moving pile with a second one if needed.
inspection_steps: Inspect each anchor point.
Check if chains, shackles, and turnbuckles are secure.
safety_warnings: The tower should always be attached to prevent it from falling over.

maintenance_steps: Stop the wind turbine by switching on the short-circuit brake before maintenance.
Brake the turbine with the brake switch before inspection.
inspection_steps: Check that the brake system is working before lowering or inspecting the turbine.
safety_warnings: Before any maintenance action, stop the wind turbine using the short-circuit brake.

maintenance_steps: Check the surrounding area of the dumpload for signs of overheating or burning.
Make sure the temperature around the dumpload is acceptable.
inspection_steps: Check if current is going into the dumpload.
Check fuses using a multimeter in continuity mode.
Check that ground and metal parts are connected correctly.
safety_warnings: Poorly tightened wires can cause fire and increase the risk of electric shock.

maintenance_steps: Connect the electrical system to the same ground rod using a ground cable to the tower.
inspection_steps: Check that grounding connections are present and secure.

maintenance_steps: Install a lightning arrester between the tower and the electronics.
inspection_steps: Check that the lightning arrester is present between the tower and electronics.
